title: Reclamation security actually posted versus a specific requirement
initial_observation: IF a mine’s operative permit or regulator decision sets a site-specific financial-security amount and due date, and a reliable dated record establishes security actually held for that obligation.
expected_observation: THEN reconcile the required security with the covered amount and instruments actually posted; distinguish any shortfall from the separate estimated reclamation liability.
possible_finding_and_basis: An evidenced unfunded required security amount can expose public cleanup risk. A liability estimate exceeding security is not automatically a breach, and an accounting provision is not a bond.
operational_join: Mine/permit ID → security requirement and amendments → actual beneficiary/instrument/site coverage. Issuer financial statements may contextualize capacity but cannot substitute for government security records.
temporal_geographic_scope: BC mine, same obligation/date/currency and permitted instrument type; separate current posted amount, statutory requirement and forecast undiscounted liability.
ordinary_explanations_and_falsifiers: ["Approved staged security or amendment", "Letter of credit/guarantee omitted from cash total", "Pooled instrument covers this site", "Different accounting discount basis", "Record predates top-up"]
mandatory_evidence: ["Operative security decision", "Dated actual-security confirmation", "Instrument conditions and beneficiary", "Site allocation for pooled security", "Relevant amendments"]
next_cheapest_check: Locate the exact site-specific requirement and an actual-held record. If either is unavailable, retain only a gated lead; do not subtract issuer provisions from liability estimates.

title: Foreign-principal money behind a specific advertised campaign
initial_observation: IF a FARA agreement/supplement itemizes a particular advertisement or campaign financed for a named foreign principal, with a sufficiently specific placement or creative reference.
expected_observation: THEN trace that placement to the archived ad and its payer/disclaimer, establishing which principal financed the message rather than treating the displayed intermediary as the ultimate sponsor.
possible_finding_and_basis: A documented financing chain can reveal whose interests a public campaign serves even when it is lawful and all disclosures are technically present.
operational_join: FARA principal/registrant/document → exact campaign/creative/placement reference → Meta ad identifier. Similar slogans, domains or spend totals are not a stable join.
temporal_geographic_scope: Actual campaign dates and covered archive geography/category; receipt, agency fee and advertising spend are different quantities.
ordinary_explanations_and_falsifiers: ["Different campaign with similar creative", "Agent paid from unrelated funds", "Disclaimer already names the principal", "Agency amount includes nonadvertising services", "Archive lacks the relevant ad class"]
mandatory_evidence: ["Original principal agreement and itemized campaign spending", "Exact ad/creative/placement crosswalk", "Full disclaimer and archived ad metadata"]
next_cheapest_check: Look for an explicit creative or placement identifier in one public FARA document; defer if the bridge is only a generic campaign description.
novelty_vs_baseline: I04 reconciles campaign spending; S05 screens sanctioned principals. This establishes message-specific financing through an intermediary without a sanctions premise.
access_status: FARA disbursement purpose/recipient fields do not guarantee a Meta creative ID. An explicit placement reference or equivalently exact documented creative bridge is mandatory; Meta archival access/coverage remains unverified.
